issues.description: No regression suite was executed (regressions_ran=0) and pov_before_reproduced=false, so functional-preservation and trigger evidence rest on code analysis rather than test execution.

getCanonicalPath containment is a well-known safe primitive but is TOCTOU-adjacent if the destination tree is concurrently manipulated; negligible for the archiver use case and no worse than the official fix.

result.root_cause: Archive entry names (e.g. containing ../ or absolute paths) are resolved against the destination dir and written without verifying the resolved path stays inside that dir, allowing extraction outside the target directory.
result.summary: Our patch inserts a canonical-path containment check at the exact shared sink (AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile, right after FileUtils.resolveFile) that the official fix targets, throwing ArchiverException when the resolved entry escapes the destination directory. It is semantically equivalent to the official fix and slightly stronger: appending File.separator and handling the f==dir case closes the /dest vs /dest-evil sibling-prefix bypass that the official startsWith check leaves open. The guard lives in the common code path all tar/zip unarchivers use, so it closes the whole traversal class rather than one payload. The only weakness is evidentiary — no regressions were run and the POV did not reproduce pre-patch — but code analysis strongly supports correctness.
